prediction_question: For a World Bank (IBRD/IDA) lending project at the moment of Board approval, will the Independent Evaluation Group's final evaluation of the project rate its outcome Moderately Satisfactory or better (MS+) on the six-point IEG outcome scale? This is an approval-instant portfolio-risk task over IEG's rated-project universe (12,629 rated projects, approval FY 1956-2024, measured 2026-10-22).
prediction_time: Board approval of the project (approval_fy / boardapprovaldate). Features may use only attributes documented by the publisher as existing at approval: approval fiscal year and Board month, agreement type, lending instrument, product line, sector and theme tags, country, region, commitment amounts, project name. Every IEG-recorded judgement is post-hoc and label-side: outcome (the label source), bank_performance, quality_at_entry, quality_of_supervision, me_quality, evaluation_fy, evaluation_type, final_closing_fy, as_of_date. Two more columns are measured to be evaluation-vintage, NOT approval-vintage, and must not ship as features: country_fcs_status and country_lending_group - 165 of 4,695 (country, approval_fy) cells carry more than one distinct FCS value across rows, and the value flips with evaluation_fy (e.g. Cameroon approval-FY-1995: P038801 evaluated 1997 -> non-FCS, P000216 evaluated 2008 -> FCS); 51 of 187 countries carry >1 FCS value across their rows. The label arrives at IEG evaluation: median 8 years after approval (min 1, max 31, measured over 12,629 rows).
target_definition: Binary from the IEG outcome rating (six-point scale: Highly Satisfactory / Satisfactory / Moderately Satisfactory / Moderately Unsatisfactory / Unsatisfactory / Highly Unsatisfactory): positive = MS+ (top three levels), negative = MU or worse. Measured mix: Satisfactory 5,639; Moderately Satisfactory 3,153; Unsatisfactory 1,870; Moderately Unsatisfactory 1,224; Highly Satisfactory 398; Highly Unsatisfactory 194; plus 151 rows 'Not Rated' which are unobserved targets, never negative labels. The label source column is outcome; the correlated IEG rating columns (bank_performance, quality_at_entry, quality_of_supervision, me_quality) are label-side and must be absent from all shipped files, not merely unlisted.

split_strategy: Temporal splits on approval fiscal year (measured on the full 12,629-row pull, 2026-10-22): train approval_fy <=2009 (n=9,741, MS+ 70.74%, 179 countries), eval 2010-2014 (n=1,488, MS+ 78.90%, 142 countries), holdout 2015-2019 (n=1,097, MS+ 80.67%, 133 countries). Both classes present in every window; the prevalence drift 70.7% -> 80.7% is a measured property of the source (IEG outcome ratings have improved over time) and must be reported beside any score, per the prevalence-shift rule. Right-censoring: rated counts fall for recent approvals (2013:269, 2015:277, 2018:184, 2021:93, 2022:56, 2023:29, 2024:11) - eligibility must iterate the provider's approval years and count unrated/not-yet-evaluated projects as unobserved_target (a bucket, not a membership decision), per the nhs-ae selection lesson. Identifier policy: project_id is unique except P122764, which appears twice (eval_fy 2023 and 2026, both ICRR, same MS rating) - construction dedupes keeping the latest evaluation_fy and declares the grain; country portfolios recur across splits by design (longitudinal), so country is a feature and the no-cross-split-entities check applies to project_id only, with expected_duplicate_ids declared in quality.json.

measurements.label_structure_2026_10_22: MS+ share over 12,478 rated rows: 0.7365. Six-level mix measured (Satisfactory 5,639 / ModSat 3,153 / ModUnsat 1,224 / Unsatisfactory 1,870 / HighlySat 398 / HighlyUnsat 194), 'Not Rated' 151. Approval-to-evaluation lag: min 1, median 8, max 31 years. Window MS+ rates: 1960-1995: 0.6999 (n=5,805); 1996-2005: 0.7199 (n=2,710); 2006-2012: 0.7465 (n=2,134); 2013-2016: 0.7980 (n=1,079); 2017-2030: 0.8009 (n=899).
measurements.provenance_mix_2026_10_22: evaluation_type is a provenance column with seven streams: ICRR 6,909 (54.7%), PPAR 3,713 (29.4%), PCR 1,482 (11.7%), EVM 487 (3.9%), PCN 35, PCM 2, CSSR 1. MS+ rate differs by stream (measured): ICRR 0.7605, PPAR 0.7266, PCR 0.6853, EVM 0.6373 - PPAR full evaluations are known to oversample problem projects, and pre-1990 rows carry the legacy PCR stream. The mixture is part of the task definition (label = latest IEG outcome rating regardless of stream) and must be declared in quality.json; a construction-time decision to restrict or keep streams must be recorded with its measured effect.
measurements.timing_vintage_finding_2026_10_22: country_fcs_status and country_lending_group are evaluation-vintage, not approval-vintage: 165 of 4,695 (country, approval_fy) cells carry >1 distinct FCS value across rows and the value tracks evaluation_fy (Cameroon approval-FY-1995: P038801 eval 1997 non-FCS, P000216 eval 2008 FCS); 51/187 countries carry >1 FCS value across rows. These columns must be excluded from shipped features (or rebuilt from a historical FCS vintage table) - a features-available-at-instant defect caught at discovery.
measurements.clustering_2026_10_22: Positives cluster weakly by borrower: 4,695 (country, approval_fy) clusters, 4,020 with >=1 MS+ positive. Per-split clustered counts to be reported at construction; the positive class (73.65%) is not a rare-event problem.

measurements.prior_art_headroom_note: The World Bank itself built this prediction model internally (Kraay & Tawara, 'Predicting IEG ratings for active projects', Policy Research Working Paper 7001, 2,729 IPF operations 1995-2012) and reports that its most predictive features - task-team-leader track record and country CPIA during the project's life - are POST-approval facts. With strictly approval-time features the achievable signal is unmeasured and may be modest; the baseline triad (majority-class 73.65% on train-window rates, calendar-only, full model) must be measured at construction before any number is quoted, and if approval-time features carry no signal beyond the majority rule the task is recorded as a negative result, not a benchmark (the nhs-ae lesson).
measurements.construction_2026_10_22: Worker job wb-001 (cx23, 385.3 s job elapsed, EUR 0.04 reservation): one anonymous IEG CSV GET (3,340,648 bytes, sha256 7080b6522bb432f0..., 1.3 s) plus 24 projects-API requests (23 offset pages of 1,000 full records + 2 supplementary id-lookup batches recovering 25 records; 54,486,121 bytes merged JSON, 22665 records). Panel: 12,629 IEG rows, P122764 deduped to its latest evaluation_fy, rated universe 12,478 with MS+ share 0.7365 (discovery anchor 0.7365). Shipped panel: train 9598 rows / 6891 positives (0.7180) / 76 distinct positive country[:10] clusters (172 untruncated countries); eval 1479 rows / 1173 positives (0.7931) / 57 distinct positive country[:10] clusters (135 untruncated countries); holdout 1097 rows / 885 positives (0.8067) / 55 distinct positive country[:10] clusters (128 untruncated countries) (approval FY windows 1956-2009 / 2010-2014 / 2015-2019). Eligibility accounted: 151 Not Rated (unobserved), 303 approved FY2020+ (outside windows, counted per year), not-yet-evaluated API projects approved <=FY2019 with no IEG row: train 1724 / eval 719 / holdout 637 (right-censoring quantified per window); api join missing after lookups: 2 ids (P072979, P113625, not served by the API); 1215 rows carry no amounts (mostly GE trust-fund records with no approval metadata). IEG-vs-API approval FY mismatches: 729 rows (+-1 FY convention; IEG CSV is canon, mismatches counted). RAP 2024 Fig O.3 cross-check: panel closing-FY MS+ FY2013 0.6875 vs FY2023 0.8729 (gap 18.5 pts; published series 71 -> 91; panel runs 3-7 pts below under every cohort restriction, trend asserted in-build). Reference baselines (stdlib, train-estimated): majority-class 0.7180; identity-only (country) 0.6003 eval / 0.4909 holdout; calendar-only (country x approval_fy) 0.6003 / 0.4909 (all eval/holdout cells unseen in train, so it falls back to identity); agreement-type rule 0.5407 / 0.4844; practice-group rule 0.5497 / 0.4948. No persistence leg exists at project grain (each project evaluated once). Gate 1.4.0 green on the worker over the full artifact (38/38 checks, artifact b8345bcb5769e422c75dd0451c81854ceb8fa809b4bb60977cd781d4071abaa9); collected to staging release 421262457 and re-verified on the coordinator with qualify_dataset.py --accept (ACCEPTED). Full-model leg of the triad: runner-contract baseline job wb-baseline-001 on the accepted artifact.
measurements.baseline_triad_2026_10_22: Runner-contract baseline wb-baseline-001 (66.9 s job elapsed, exit 0; the five accepted files fetched from staging 421262457, re-ACCEPTed before scoring, runner files verbatim and hash-matched): train.py eval AUC 0.5879, validate.py independent recompute 0.5879, CONTRACT OK. THE FULL TRIAD ON THE SAME EVAL ROWS: majority-class rule 0.718 accuracy (constant AUC 0.5); identity-only country rate rule 0.6003 eval / 0.4909 holdout; calendar-only (country x approval_fy, cells unseen in train so it falls back to identity) 0.6003 / 0.4909; full model 0.5879 eval. DEFECT RECORDED: the contract model TRAILS the one-line country-identity rule on eval by 0.0124 AUC - per dataset-qualification this is a recorded defect, not an encouraging result, and no headroom claim may be quoted from the model number alone. Two open facts temper the verdict and name the decisive missing number: (1) the identity rule INVERTS on holdout (0.4909, below chance - the country priors go stale across the prevalence shift 0.718 -> 0.807), while the model's HOLDOUT AUC was not measured by the contract job (the runner scores holdout via bench eval, not the baseline contract); (2) the model gap is 0.0124 on one default-contract run, not a measured ceiling. Next session must score the same runner model and the identity rule on the HOLDOUT rows before any benchmark-or-negative verdict: if the model holds ~0.59 while identity sits at 0.49, the task discriminates where it is scored and the defect is an eval-window artifact of stale priors; if the model also collapses, the candidate is a negative result and drops per the one-rebuild budget.
measurements.holdout_comparison_2026_10_23: Job wb-holdout-001 (staging release 421361824; gate accept BEFORE scoring; xgboost 3.4.1 / scikit-learn 1.9.1 / pandas 2.3.3 / numpy 2.5.4 / python 3.13.17). Eval (FY2010-2014, 1,479 rows, prevalence 0.7931): model AUC 0.5879 (brier 0.1703) [reproduces wb-baseline-001 0.5879], identity-country rule 0.6003 (0.1740) [reproduces build's early-scored value], calendar-trend (logistic on approval_fy + cyclical month, train-fitted, non-degenerate) 0.5209 (0.1717), prior-share rule 0.5783 (0.1807), majority-class accuracy measured 0.7931. Holdout (FY2015-2019, 1,097 rows, prevalence 0.8067): model AUC 0.5301 (brier 0.1757), identity rule 0.4909 (0.1869) [reproduces build's early-scored 0.4909], calendar-trend 0.4780 (0.1668), prior-share 0.4938 (0.1929), majority-class accuracy measured 0.8067. Paired cluster bootstrap by country (2,000 resamples, seed 20261023, 0 skipped): holdout model-identity delta +0.0393 CI [-0.0113, +0.0899]; model-calendar +0.0522 CI [-0.0236, +0.1296]; model-prior +0.0364 CI [-0.0151, +0.0811]; eval model-identity -0.0124 CI [-0.0506, +0.0309]; eval model-calendar +0.0670 CI [+0.0052, +0.1261] (the only interval excluding zero, on the split the runner does not score). Per-year holdout model AUC: 2015 0.5146, 2016 0.5778, 2017 0.5361, 2018 0.5030, 2019 0.5071; identity rule per year declines 0.4908 -> 0.4408. Prevalence shift documented: 0.7180 -> 0.7931 -> 0.8067. Empirically confirmed: the build's country x approval_fy table falls back to country identity on 100% of eval and holdout rows (scores bit-identical to the identity rule) - the Codex calendar-degeneracy finding, now measured, not assumed. Information sets verified by perturbation for identity (reads only country), calendar (only approval_fy + approval_month_num), prior-share (only prior_msplus_share + prior_evals_count); all non-claimed non-constant columns row-shuffled with scores bit-identical. AUC computed by two independent implementations (tie-averaged Mann-Whitney and sklearn), agreement asserted 1e-9. Commands: bundle candidates/wb-ieg-project-outcome/holdout (assembled via scripts/assemble-job.py wb-holdout), sh scripts/scout-factory worker plan|launch, collect; every number above is read from output/holdout-comparison.json in release 421361824. Scope note: the full-model holdout figure comes from the runner's own predict_proba in this one job (fresh deterministic fit of the fixed train.py config); it was not re-derived by a second modelling implementation. The AUC arithmetic is dual-implemented (tie-averaged Mann-Whitney vs sklearn, agreement asserted 1e-9) and the identity-rule figures WERE independently replicated from the written bytes (this job's pandas implementation matching build.py's stdlib loop to 4 dp).

artifacts.note: wb-001 build: gated extract (public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json, quality.json), build summary (two byte-identical copies), the gate report (two byte-identical copies, sha256 c68e34c8...), source.tar and container.log; artifact digest b8345bcb5769e422c75dd0451c81854ceb8fa809b4bb60977cd781d4071abaa9

rejection_reason: DROP (status dropped), decisive evidence: the one bounded holdout job the record called for (wb-holdout-001, staging release 421361824, exit 0, 57.3 s, gate --accept BEFORE scoring: 'ACCEPTED: /data/extract matches the qualified artifact b8345bcb5769e422') measured the missing decisive number and it does not support a benchmark claim. On the runner-scored holdout (approval FY 2015-2019, 1,097 rows, 885 positives, prevalence 0.8067): the runner-contract model (benchmark train.py verbatim via runpy, same fitted model as wb-baseline-001, no retraining choices) scores AUC 0.5301 - near chance - and is statistically indistinguishable from the train-fitted country rate-table rule at 0.4909: paired cluster bootstrap by country (2,000 resamples, fixed seed) delta AUC +0.0393, 95% CI [-0.0113, +0.0899] - the interval contains zero, so 'the model beats the rule where the runner scores' is NOT demonstrated. The same holds against the genuine time-only calendar control (logistic on approval_fy + cyclical month, train-fitted: AUC 0.4780; delta +0.0522, CI [-0.0236, +0.1296], contains zero) and the prior-track-record rule (prior_msplus_share with base-rate fallback: AUC 0.4938; delta +0.0364, CI [-0.0151, +0.0811], contains zero). The earlier adverse eval comparison is kept, not replaced: on eval (FY 2010-2014, 1,479 rows) the model 0.5879 trails the identity rule 0.6003 (delta -0.0124, CI [-0.0506, +0.0309], contains zero); the model does beat the calendar control on eval (+0.0670, CI [+0.0052, +0.1261]) but that does not carry to the split the runner scores. Diagnosis within the one bounded repair (no implementation defect found: acceptance preceded scoring; the model reproduces wb-baseline-001's eval AUC 0.5879 exactly; the identity rule reproduces the build's early-scored 0.6003/0.4909 exactly from the written bytes - an independent replication; dual AUC implementations agree to 1e-9; every reference's information set verified by perturbation - all non-claimed columns row-shuffled, scores bit-identical): the failure is in the task's signal, not the code. The country track-record rule INVERTS on holdout (0.4909, worsening per year to 0.4408 by 2019) while prevalence shifts 0.7180 (train) -> 0.7931 (eval) -> 0.8067 (holdout); the model itself decays eval 0.5879 -> holdout 0.5301; no holdout year shows model AUC above 0.578. Per dataset-qualification: no demonstrated headroom under this protocol; the negative finding is preserved with both scores on identical rows; one repair was budgeted and spent; a second rebuild is not warranted because the defect is task design (an approval-instant portfolio whose outcome signal does not survive to the 2015-2019 cohort), not construction. Re-scope, if ever reopened, means a NEW task instance (e.g. a change/onset target or a different label horizon) with its own qualification - never a re-tuned threshold on this one. This drop also closes the Codex source-review items against any release from this candidate: nothing will be packaged or published from it, so the latest-vintage prior-history claim (evaluation_fy from the current IEG snapshot, not a point-in-time reconstruction) ships nowhere; the degenerate country x approval_fy 'calendar' control was empirically confirmed (100% of eval/holdout keys fall back to country identity, scores bit-identical to the identity rule) and replaced in the final measurement by a genuine time-only control; the mislabeled majority_class_accuracy field (training prevalence restated as split accuracy) is superseded by the measured per-split values (eval 0.7931, holdout 0.8067 - each split's own prevalence, measured as a constant prediction, distinct from train 0.7180).

Disposition in this candidate: the first three were re-measured and closed by wb-holdout-001 (accept-before-score ordering; per-split measured accuracy; degeneracy empirically confirmed at fallback fraction 1.0 and replaced by a genuine time-only control); the fourth is moot for release because the candidate is dropped and nothing ships - recorded as a limitation any future instance must state as an assumption, never a point-in-time reconstruction.

prior_art: Kraay & Tawara, World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 7001 (2014), predicting IEG ratings for active IPF projects; Goldemberg, Jordan & Kenyon, WPS 10532 (2023); lukesjordan/worldbank-project-documents on Hugging Face (documents, no splits)
novelty_check.theirs: The World Bank publishes the ratings data itself (CC BY 4.0) and built an internal prediction model (Kraay & Tawara, WPS 7001: 2,729 IPF operations 1995-2012, features include post-approval TTL track record and CPIA, no public artifact); Goldemberg et al. WPS 10532 (2023) use ML on project documents to predict contribution to sector outcomes, not ratings; Hugging Face hosts World Bank project documents (lukesjordan/worldbank-project-documents, 15.7k docs) whose card says 'no leaderboard yet' and 'we have not done a train test split'; no public train/eval/holdout task with a scored contract on this source was found
novelty_check.ours: A packaged approval-instant binary task over IEG's rated-project universe (12,629 rated projects, approval FY 1956-2024, CC BY 4.0): at Board approval, predict whether IEG's final evaluation rates the outcome MS+, with strictly approval-time features (the evaluation-vintage FCS/lending-group columns measured and excluded), temporal splits by approval FY (train <=2009 n=9,741 / eval 2010-2014 n=1,488 / holdout 2015-2019 n=1,097), unobserved-target accounting for not-yet-evaluated approvals, provenance-stream declaration (ICRR/PPAR/PCR/EVM), and the runner's scored contract
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
